clue.text: School breaks near plant

indicators.note: the school breaks into, or splits apart, the word for near, sitting in its middle

parts.note: by means near, as in standing by the door
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school holiday is spent close to some industrial plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Betony is a purple-flowered herb of the mint family, long used medicinally.

clue.text: Swimming round ship, cat in sea requires help

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for a ship
swimming suggests the following letters moving about freely and rearranging

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
SS stands for steamship before a vessel's name

explanation.surface: A cat that has fallen overboard and is swimming round a ship needs rescuing.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance and help are straightforward synonyms for aid given to someone.

clue.text: Old statesman is taking regular slices of bread into shop

indicators.note: the letters so far are put into the word for a shop, splitting it

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a kind of shop

indicators.note: the little word is takes on the following letters straight after it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: regular slices means taking every other letter of the word bread

explanation.surface: Someone takes evenly cut slices of bread into a sandwich shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular slices of' bread takes its second and fourth letters, RA; IS plus RA goes into DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a nineteenth-century British Conservative prime minister.

clue.text: Writer's dog

definitions.meaning: The English novelist of the Regeneration trilogy
a dog is something that barks, hence one who barks

explanation.surface: This seems to name the pet belonging to some author.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat Barker the novelist, and a barking animal is literally one that barks.

clue.text: Bags from which beer initially runs

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word beer is taken

parts.note: runs in tights or stockings are ladders in British English

explanation.surface: Containers from which beer starts to flow.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a run in a stocking is called a ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bladder is an inflatable sac or bag, as in a football bladder.

clue.text: Editors, furious about review, finally becoming most unruly

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, or around, the picked letter
furious suggests the letters thrashing about wildly into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: finally takes only the last letter of the word review

explanation.surface: Editors angered by a bad notice end up behaving as badly as anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' scrambles EDITORS around W, the last letter of review given by 'finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy means noisy and disorderly, so its superlative is the most disorderly or unruly.

clue.text: Writer is greeting spiritual leader, not entirely old

parts.note: taken as written
hi is an informal greeting

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is left off the word for a spiritual leader

parts.note: a guru is a Hindu spiritual teacher

explanation.surface: An author says hello to a religious teacher who is not quite elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Kazuo Ishiguro is the Nobel-winning author of The Remains of the Day.

clue.text: No more than four, not for opt-out

indicators.note: not says the letters of the word for are removed from the word four

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be taken away

indicators.note: out signals the letters of opt being put out of order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A limit of four people is set, rather than letting everyone choose to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking F, O, R from FOUR leaves U; 'out' turns OPT into PTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to is an idiom setting a maximum, as in up to four guests allowed.

clue.text: Writer took risks, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An author was somewhat daring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Okri is the Nigerian-born novelist who won the Booker Prize for The Famished Road.

clue.text: Writer, a figure in the red

parts.note: two is a figure, a number
being in the red means overdrawn, abbreviated OD on statements

explanation.surface: An author finds a sum in debt on the bank statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Atwood is the Canadian novelist of The Handmaid's Tale.

clue.text: Flier, deserter, or a deserting flier?

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter jet, so a flier
a rat is one who deserts, as rats leave a sinking ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a pilot who walks out is a deserter or just a flier who has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A migratory bird leaves its home for another region each season, so it is a flier that departs.

clue.text: Shot directly at a number of farm animals

indicators.note: shot means broken or ruined, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fires straight at a herd of livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy cattle are cows kept for their milk, a herd of livestock on a farm.

clue.text: Improve material with one gutless novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: gutless means the inside letter is removed, leaving just the outer ones

explanation.surface: Someone wants to make the material of a weak novel better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' reduces ONE to OE; 'novel' rearranges MATERIAL plus OE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to make something better, a formal synonym for improving it.

clue.text: Finally submitting account the wrong way, drinks from Paris and London follow

indicators.note: the drinks follow the account, coming after it
the wrong way means the abbreviation for account is turned round

parts.note: vin is French for wine, a drink of Paris
gin is the drink of London, as in London dry gin

explanation.surface: After a bill is botched, wine and gin are brought out in France and England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns AC into CA.
explanation.definitionFit: Caving in is an idiom for finally yielding or giving way under pressure.

clue.text: Luton's foremost orchestra breaking into music etc, a hotchpotch

indicators.note: the letters break into the word for music and the like, splitting it

parts.note: music and similar pursuits are the arts

indicators.note: foremost takes only the first letter of Luton

parts.note: LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: Luton's leading orchestra bursts into the music scene with a medley.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is an English town north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An allsorts is a varied mixture of different things, like the liquorice sweets of that name.

clue.text: Writer needs race to stop

parts.note: to rush is to race along
to die is to stop working, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: An author must hurry to halt something.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie is the British-Indian author of Midnight's Children.

clue.text: Dog gets to perform with parent in capital city

parts.note: to do is to perform an action

indicators.note: the parent sits in the name of the capital

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A dog gets to put on a show with its mother in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dobermann is a large German breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Writer in a cryptic crossword setter

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the short words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged
Paul is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter

explanation.surface: The setter of this very puzzle is said to be an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the name under which this Guardian crossword's setter publishes.
explanation.definitionFit: V S Naipaul was the Trinidad-born Nobel laureate author of A House for Mr Biswas.

clue.text: Attendants semi-dressed, including daughter in plaits

indicators.note: the jumbled group sits in the word for plaits

parts.note: braids are plaits of hair

indicators.note: the rearranged letters include the abbreviation for daughter inside them
dressed suggests the letters being dressed, arranged in a new way

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Half-dressed attendants at a wedding, including the bride's daughter, have their hair in plaits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' rearranges SEMI; with D 'including', it makes IDESM, which goes into BRAIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridesmaids are the women or girls who attend a bride at her wedding.

clue.text: Writer's rodents, one less pale

indicators.note: less says the letter for one is taken out of the rodents

parts.note: mice are small rodents
I is the Roman numeral for one
wan means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: An author's pet rodents, one fewer and looking peaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian McEwan is the English novelist of Atonement and Amsterdam.

clue.text: All concluding sudoku is done and spent

indicators.note: all concluding means the last letter of every one of the following words

explanation.surface: Finishing a sudoku leaves someone exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent and used both describe something exhausted or consumed, like a used cartridge.

clue.text: Writer improperly abridged

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: amiss means wrongly or improperly, as in to take something amiss

explanation.surface: An author's work has been cut badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley Amis, and his son Martin, are celebrated English novelists.

clue.text: Dark gold, reversible hat

parts.note: sombre means dark and gloomy

indicators.note: reversible says the word for gold is turned backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A dark gold hat that can be worn inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, the heraldic word for gold, is turned by 'reversible' into RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Writer's report of fast food

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word sounds like a fast food

parts.note: a burger is a staple of fast food

explanation.surface: An author's account of eating junk food.
explanation.definitionFit: John Berger was the English art critic and novelist, author of Ways of Seeing and G.

clue.text: Aversion evident ultimately in almost total catastrophe

indicators.note: the final letter goes in the shortened catastrophe
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a total catastrophe is a disaster

indicators.note: ultimately takes only the last letter of evident

explanation.surface: Someone's dislike is plain at the end of an almost complete calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts DISASTER to DISASTE, and 'ultimately' gives the T of evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of dislike or mild repugnance, a synonym of aversion.

clue.text: Writer's report of farm buildings

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word sounds like the buildings

parts.note: barns are large farm buildings for storing crops

explanation.surface: An author's account of agricultural structures.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Barnes is the English novelist who won the Booker Prize for The Sense of an Ending.
